abstract.text:
We argue that BPS ansatzes, entering manifestly vacuum BPS monopole solutions to equations of
motion in the (Minkowskian) non-Abelian Higgs model play the role of some electric form-factors and
that this implies (soft) violating the CP-invariance of the mentioned model, similar to taking place
in the Euclidian Yang-Mills (YM) theory with instantons, generating the θ-term in the appropriate
effective Hamiltonian.

sections.summary: Introduces the Minkowskian Yang-Mills-Higgs model, its BPS limit, the Bogomol’nyi equation and bound, and vacuum BPS monopole solutions. It develops the superfluid helium II analogy for the BPS monopole vacuum and contrasts this with ’t Hooft-Polyakov monopoles, where the analogous superfluid/form-factor effects are absent.

sections.summary: Repeats Witten-style arguments on CP conservation and dyon charge quantization, then introduces the instanton θ-term as the standard CP-violating linear term. It argues that the BPS ansatz f1BP S produces an analogous CP-violating effect without any θ-dependence, arising from tree-level rather than loop Feynman diagrams.

sections.summary: Shows that Dirac fundamental quantization of the YMH BPS vacuum yields a rotary action functional that is both P-invariant and C-invariant. This contrasts with the instanton θ-vacuum and is presented as a remarkable feature of the BPS-monopole model.

abstract.text:
We argue that BPS ansatzes, entering manifestly vacuum BPS monopole solutions to equations of
motion in the (Minkowskian) non-Abelian Higgs model play the role of some electric form-factors and
that this implies (soft) violating the CP-invariance of the mentioned model, similar to taking place
in the Euclidian Yang-Mills (YM) theory with instantons, generating the θ-term in the appropriate
effective Hamiltonian.

sections.summary: Introduces the Minkowskian Yang-Mills-Higgs model, its BPS limit, the Bogomol’nyi equation and bound, and vacuum BPS monopole solutions. It develops the superfluid helium II analogy for the BPS monopole vacuum and contrasts this with ’t Hooft-Polyakov monopoles, where the analogous superfluid/form-factor effects are absent.

It argues that the BPS ansatz f1BP S produces an analogous CP-violating effect without any θ-dependence, arising from tree-level rather than loop Feynman diagrams.
